entries.sense_en: travelling across or along a place

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and general; traverse is formal and suggests covering a long or difficult stretch.
Plain wording; says nothing about going from one side to the other.
Neutral; often a quick movement over something rather than a whole route.

entries.sense_en: the triangular upper part of a wall at the end of a sloping roof

synonyms.nuance: A triangular part above a door or columns in classical buildings; more decorative than a gable.
synonyms.example: a pediment over the temple entrance

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for the top point of a roof, not the whole triangular wall.
synonyms.example: birds sitting on the roof peak

entries.sense_en: moving around a place quietly and watchfully, looking for something

synonyms.nuance: Wandering freely with no purpose; prowl suggests searching or hunting.
Waiting hidden, often with bad intent; prowl keeps moving.
Relaxed, happy walking; prowl is tense and purposeful.

entries.sense_en: attractive in an old-fashioned, unusual way

synonyms.nuance: Pleasing in general; not necessarily old-fashioned.
Looks like a painting; about scenery or views more than small old details.
Just out of date; can be neutral or negative, while quaint is warm.

entries.sense_en: sharing the same interests and easy to be with

synonyms.nuance: Able to work or live together without conflict; more neutral, also used for things.
Pleasant and easy to please; does not stress shared tastes.
Everyday word for warm behavior; congenial is more formal and about being a good match.

entries.sense_en: walked slowly and threateningly, like a hunter or an evil figure

synonyms.nuance: Long, confident steps; not necessarily menacing.
Slow and quiet, often frightening; stalk is more deliberate and powerful.
Keep appearing in a place, like a ghost; stalk moves with purpose.

entries.sense_en: polite and generous toward women and the weak, like a knight

synonyms.nuance: Brave, and courteous to women; slightly old-fashioned.
Everyday word for polite, respectful male behavior.
Politeness in general; not tied to gender or honor.

entries.sense_en: a soft, gentle wind

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary word for a light wind; zephyr is poetic.
A sudden, stronger burst of wind, the opposite of a zephyr.

entries.sense_en: a foolish or useless person, here said half-jokingly of an old man

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more general insult for a stupid person.
Specifically an old person with outdated ideas.
Someone who keeps making clumsy mistakes.

entries.sense_en: struck down with a serious illness (past tense: smote)

synonyms.nuance: Common word for hitting or a sudden bad event; smite is literary and forceful.
Cause long suffering, usually by illness; the effect lasts.
Plain, everyday word; lacks the feeling of fate or punishment.

entries.sense_en: the whole collection of medicines a doctor can use
entries.sense_ko: 약전, (의사가 쓸 수 있는) 약물 전체

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for drugs or the science of treating illness.
Treatments of any kind, including home cures.

entries.sense_en: has firmly decided something

synonyms.nuance: Plain verb; make up one’s mind stresses that the choice is settled after thought.
Stronger: a decision one will stubbornly act on.
Formal; a firm decision, often about future action.

entries.sense_en: nonsense! (an old-fashioned exclamation)

synonyms.nuance: Standard word; works in any register.
British, informal; rejects an idea as worthless.
Informal, American; often for exaggerated or untrue talk.

entries.sense_en: walked in a boldly confident way, hiding her worry

synonyms.nuance: Stiff, proud walk to show off; swagger is looser and more careless.
Long, purposeful steps without any show-off feeling.
Slow, relaxed walk with no hurry.

entries.sense_en: make a path to future success by doing early, smaller work

synonyms.nuance: Do the groundwork so something can happen later.
Create a chance; less about slow, step-by-step work.
synonyms.example: It opened the door to a career.

synonyms.nuance: Build the basic base for something bigger.

entries.sense_en: in a caring, worried way

synonyms.nuance: Stresses fear or nervousness, not care for another.
Simple and warm; solicitously adds a worried, attentive tone.
Gentle and loving in touch or voice.

entries.sense_en: twisted and rough with age, like an old tree

synonyms.nuance: Bent out of shape; no idea of age or roughness.
Full of knots; describes wood texture more than age.
Worn by sun and rain; smoother than gnarled.

entries.sense_en: a strong feeling that something is silly or worthless

synonyms.nuance: Deep, serious feeling that someone or something is worthless.
Cool, proud dislike, often from feeling superior.
Openly making fun; scorn can stay silent.

entries.sense_en: let go of something completely

synonyms.nuance: The everyday form; also used for feelings.
Formal; free something that was held.
Stop trying; suggests defeat, not just loosening the grip.

entries.sense_en: held and used (a tool) skillfully

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and general; wield suggests skill or force.
Manage by hand; less dramatic, works for many things.
Wave threateningly or to show off, not to work with.

entries.sense_en: a clumsy, poorly made painting
entries.sense_ko: 서툴게 그린 그림, 덕지덕지 칠한 그림

synonyms.nuance: Careless writing or drawing with a pen or pencil.
A dirty mark spread on a surface; not a picture.
A quick drawing, not necessarily bad.

entries.sense_en: a big, strong guard dog

synonyms.nuance: Any dog kept to guard a place; also a person who protects.
Trained to protect; common everyday phrase.
A different breed, short and stubborn; used for tough people.

entries.tip_ko: mastiff-in-waiting은 lady-in-waiting(시녀)을 비튼 농담: 두 화가를 곁에서 지키는 충견 노릇.

entries.sense_en: easily broken or harmed

synonyms.nuance: Fine and easily damaged; often positive, about beauty or care.
Weak in body, mostly said of old or sick people.
Badly made and weak; negative.

entries.sense_en: a strange idea that one imagines

synonyms.nuance: A vague idea or belief, often a little odd.
A false belief that one truly holds; stronger and more serious.
A sudden wish with no reason.

entries.sense_en: open laughter or mockery showing something is foolish

synonyms.nuance: Making fun of someone in words; very close, more common.
Copying or teasing to make fun.
An inner feeling of no respect, not necessarily shown by laughing.

entries.sense_en: annoying (a mild, old-fashioned swear word)

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned mild curse; angry and informal.
Stronger curse word.
Neutral, polite description of what bothers you.

entries.sense_en: unhealthily fixed on sad or dark thoughts, especially death
entries.sense_ko: 병적인, 죽음 같은 어두운 생각에 사로잡힌

synonyms.nuance: Sad or dark in mood; less extreme, not necessarily about death.
Frightening because of death or horror; about things, not minds.
General; morbid points to the mind’s dark focus.

entries.sense_en: a silly, chattering person who cannot be serious

synonyms.nuance: Someone forgetful and unable to focus.
A person who talks too much; not necessarily silly.
Modern slang for a foolish person; ruder.

entries.sense_en: looked closely and carefully, because it was hard to see or scary

synonyms.nuance: Long, steady look, often with wonder or feeling.
A very quick look.
Look with half-closed eyes, from bright light or poor eyesight.
Look fixedly and openly, sometimes rudely.

entries.sense_en: look! (used to introduce something surprising)

synonyms.nuance: Also archaic and solemn; a verb meaning ‘look at’.
Everyday way to draw attention.
Fixed phrase still used today, often humorously, to introduce a surprise.
synonyms.example: And lo and behold, it worked!

entries.sense_en: sudden strong rushes of wind

synonyms.nuance: Light, steady, pleasant wind.
A very strong burst of wind or air.
A sudden storm with wind and rain.

entries.sense_en: whole, from beginning to end (used for emphasis)

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for the whole thing; no feeling of a slow, long time.
Everyday; livelong stresses how long it feels.
Describes an event that lasts all night.

entries.sense_en: having a jagged edge like a saw

synonyms.nuance: Rough and uneven with sharp points; not regular like teeth.
Plain description of edges with small points.
Cut with small V-shaped nicks.

entries.sense_en: the process of breaking down and falling apart

synonyms.nuance: Slow rotting or wearing away; the most common word here.
Breaking into small pieces.
Sudden falling down or failing.

entries.sense_en: moved lightly and quickly, like a bird’s wings

synonyms.nuance: Bigger, louder movement, often of wings or cloth.
Tiny, fast trembling, often from feeling.
Slow back-and-forth movement.

entries.sense_en: (of time) slowly passed

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for time moving on.
Time feels slow and boring.
Time passes, often without notice.

entries.sense_en: made quick, light tapping sounds as it fell

synonyms.nuance: Falls in single drops; no repeated tapping sound.
Heavier, louder, regular beat.
One knock at a time, often by a person.

entries.sense_en: (of an illness) sudden and severe

synonyms.nuance: Very serious; does not say the illness came suddenly.
Happening quickly; does not say how serious.
Life may be in danger.
